title: Operator and Operand
definition: An operator denotes an operation, while its operands are the values or expressions to which that operation is applied.
purpose: Make value-producing operations and their inputs explicit.
history: Programming languages use operator notation to express common unary, binary, and assignment-related operations compactly.
mental_model: An operator is a rule-bearing machine; operands enter with types and values, and evaluation produces a value or effect.
analogy: A calculator key acts on entered values; the analogy fails when language operators coerce types, short-circuit, or create effects.
common_mistakes: Treating one symbol as one universal operation
industry_notes: Expression review should expose operand types, conversion boundaries, and intended grouping.
ai_notes: AI-generated expressions must be expanded into typed intermediate results and tested at boundaries.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to name each operator, operand, intermediate type, and result.
exercise_candidates: Annotate compound expressions with operand types
project_candidates: Make transformations explicit in a console pipeline
